label: prop:pn-averaging-uniqueness
title: Bar-invariant p-n interface averagings
html:
Let R be a field, q \in R with q \neq 0 and q^{2}+1 \neq 0, and write z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) and h = q - q^{-1}. For a function c, consider the p-n interface averaging \sigma_{c} = z - c\,h. Then \sigma_c is bar-invariant at q,

  \sigma_{c}(q) = \sigma_{c}(q^{-1}),

if and only if \bigl(c(q) + c(q^{-1}) - 1\bigr)\,h = 0. In particular, if c is constant and h \neq 0, bar-invariance forces 2c = 1: the uniform form z - h/2 is the only bar-invariant member with constant coefficient.

Proof

Under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} one has \overline{h} = -h and \overline{z} = z - h, since q^{-3}/(q^{-2}+1) = 1/(q(q^{2}+1)) = z - h. Hence \overline{\sigma_c} = z - h + \overline{c}\,h, and \sigma_c - \overline{\sigma_c} = (c + \overline{c} - 1)\,h. For constant c this is (2c-1)\,h, which vanishes with h \neq 0 only when 2c = 1. \square

The result does not single out a canonical averaging. A q-dependent coefficient with c + \overline{c} = 1 is also bar-invariant, so uniqueness holds only among constant coefficients.

Setting

The QOU mass identity at A \geq 2 contracts a per-interface averaging functional \sigma_{pn} across the p-n boundary slice. The two production candidates are the uniform bar-invariant form z - h/2 and the Bring color-tube weighted form z - h(1/2 - \delta/4).

Scope. Only the uniform form satisfies bar-invariance. Writing \overline{\phantom{x}} for q \mapsto q^{-1}, the flavour split is bar-mixed, \overline{\delta} = -q^{2}\delta, and

  \overline{\sigma_{pn}^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}} - \sigma_{pn}^{\,\mathrm{weighted}}
  \;=\; \frac{(q-1)^{5}(q+1)^{3}(q^{2}+1)}{12\,q^{5}}
  \;\neq\; 0
  \quad (q \neq 1),

about 1.67 \times 10^{-5} at the substrate anchor, whereas the uniform form is bar-invariant exactly — it is the bar-symmetriser \tfrac12(z + \overline{z}) of the p-p factor, since \overline{z} = z - h (Proof of interface knot markov z).

The colour-weighted coefficient c = 1/2 - \delta/4 depends on q and has c + \overline{c} - 1 = -\delta(1-q^{2})/4 \neq 0, which is the computation above.

The consequence is one of scope: the uniqueness statement covers constant coefficients, and the colour-weighted convention lies outside its hypotheses. This does not say the colour weighting is wrong, and it does not by itself bear on which convention should be canonical.

Derivation chain for the closed-form weight

The substrate evaluation w(t, t', q) = 1/(1 - h_q \cdot q^{10}) derives from Bring's surface geometry:

  • Bring's surface has genus g = 4.
  • The genus-4 force-carrier pair is \{T(2,9), T(3,5)\}.
  • \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T_{p,k}) = k \cdot (p-1). For T(3,5), \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T(3,5)) = 10. This specifies the pole order of \sigma.
  • The Bring color-tube weight inherits this derived pole order q^{10}.

All statements above are proved: \overline{z} = z - h for z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1), the bar-invariance criterion, the uniqueness among constant coefficients, and the bar-invariance of z - h/2. In addition, two averagings with the same 9-pair colour weight agree. Choosing that weight is open.
